patterns.interactionStrategy: click container -> fill search input -> await options -> click active result item
evaluate DOM removal (#kdn-welcome-modal, .modal-backdrop) -> reset body overflow

patterns.component: Async Multi-Popup Overlay & Don't Show Again Checkbox
patterns.interactionStrategy: check 'Don't show again' input if present -> count and click visible close buttons -> strip #multi-popup-overlay from DOM -> reset body overflow

patterns.component: Header & Footer Navigation Strict Mode Disambiguation
patterns.interactionStrategy: append .first() to locator getters in POM classes to resolve strict mode collisions across header/footer links

Never combine a page-specific class/id selector with a generic attribute selector (e.g. button[type="submit"]) in one comma-separated locator when calling .first(). The generic half can match an unrelated element earlier in DOM order. Use the specific selector alone, or scope the generic one to its containing form (e.g. form.login-form button[type="submit"]).
patterns.notes: Real incident: 'button.login-button, button[type="submit"]'.first() silently clicked the storefront header search button instead of Sign In!, saving an unauthenticated storageState with no exception thrown. See pattern-library.md ANTI-005.

patterns.component: Treating 'No Exception Thrown' as Proof of Success
patterns.interactionStrategy: Any code that establishes state via a UI action other code depends on (auth login writing storageState, a wizard step advancing, a payment submitting) MUST verify the outcome via an unambiguous signal (session cookie, specific post-action URL, authenticated-only DOM element) before treating it as success. 'Didn't throw' is not proof of success.
patterns.notes: Same incident as ANTI-005 — the click succeeded silently, so a broken login was saved as a 'successful' auth state for every downstream test to inherit. See pattern-library.md ANTI-006.

patterns.component: Page-Exists Screenshot As Proof of Claimed Backend Effect
patterns.interactionStrategy: When a requirement claims 'admin sees X data after a customer does Y', Stage 4 (Live Explorer) must perform the write action (Y) first, THEN navigate to the claimed admin page and confirm a row matching that specific record's identifying data is visible — not just that the page loads with plausible column headers.
patterns.notes: REQ-07 (b2b-registration): the 'confirmed real location' from Stage 4 exploration showed 'No records' in its own screenshot. Real location was /Admin/ErpAccount/List, found only via manual live investigation. See pattern-library.md ANTI-007.

patterns.component: Fixed-Delay 'Wait for Another Process to Flush' Guards
patterns.interactionStrategy: Never assume a fixed delay (e.g. setTimeout(r, 1000)) is 'long enough' for another process to finish writing a file this code depends on. Prefer a deterministic check (e.g. compare the JSON reporter's own invocation argv against the current process's argv) polled with a bounded timeout, and log a visible warning if it times out.
patterns.notes: 1000ms fixed sleep before reading test-results.json wasn't always enough under load; custom report silently regenerated from stale data (once showing 0% right after a 100% pass run). Residual limitation noted in pattern-library.md ANTI-008: --headed runs with trace/video can still exceed any reasonable synchronous wait.
patterns.confidenceCaveat: Heuristic-based, not a hard guarantee — see notes.

patterns.component: Per-Test Timeout Budget Ignoring Nested Browser Contexts
patterns.interactionStrategy: When a test opens additional browser.newContext()s beyond the primary page fixture (e.g. a withAdminPage()-style helper), Agent 4 (Codegen) must apply test.setTimeout() sized for (primary flow) + (per extra context: navigation + auth-state load + assertions) rather than relying on the suite's blanket default. Agent 5 should treat many different tests failing at the same early step inside a shared multi-context helper as a timeout-budget signal, not diagnose each test's locators independently.
patterns.notes: 7 tests using withAdminPage() or a full 3-step form submission exceeded the 30s default timeout once the auth fix (ANTI-005/006) made the admin flow actually run. See pattern-library.md ANTI-009.
